analysis.one_liner: DLF is India's largest listed real-estate developer, building and selling homes (mostly luxury, concentrated around Gurugram) while also earning steady rental income from offices and malls through its DCCDL joint venture.
analysis.whats_happening: DLF declared Q2 FY27 (quarter to September 2026) results on 16 October 2026: consolidated PAT of ₹1,301 crore, up 11% YoY, alongside a ₹8 per share dividend. New sales bookings (pre-sales) came in at ₹3,800 crore for the quarter - a small slice of the ₹20,000 crore full-year FY27 target management has guided to, so the next two quarters need a sharp pickup from planned launches (Hamilton Court 2, Goa villas, Mumbai Westpark Phase 2). The board also approved reclassifying promoter entity Madhukar Housing to the public category, pending exchange approval.
analysis.plain_terms: Think of DLF as two businesses stitched together: a home-building arm that books lumpy, launch-dependent revenue, and a rental arm (DCCDL) that collects steady, growing rent from offices and malls. The home-building side needs a big second half to hit its sales target; the rental side is quietly doing most of the heavy lifting on profit stability right now. That split matters because a buyer looking only at the revenue or profit headline would miss which part is actually driving the number.
analysis.quarters: Consolidated revenue of ₹2,297 crore in Q2 FY27 was down sharply versus the year-ago quarter, but this is not a clean like-for-like comparison - real-estate revenue is booked on project completion/possession milestones, and last year's quarter carried a large recognition tied to The Dahlias handovers. PAT still rose 11% YoY to ₹1,301 crore because the DCCDL rental annuity business (₹1,482 crore rental income, ₹1,537 crore EBITDA, 96% occupancy by area) kept growing steadily. The more reliable quarterly health check is new sales bookings, which at ₹3,800 crore in Q2 are well behind the pace needed for the ₹20,000 crore FY27 target management has reiterated.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is 33.3% below its all-time peak of ₹1,011.51 - but that peak was set in January 2008, a listing-era bubble high just months after DLF's July 2007 IPO, not a recent crash. There has been no split or demerger (has_corporate_action: false), so the raw price series needs no adjustment here. Over more relevant horizons the picture flips: 3-year return of +25.4% and 5-year return of +69.8% both beat the Nifty (+18.0%, +25.3%) and dramatically beat peer Godrej Properties (-1.9%, -32.3%). The 1-year return of -11.7% is roughly in line with the Nifty's -10.7% and far better than the peer's -29.4%. The stock currently sits mid-range between its 52-week low (₹497.85) and high (₹769.83).
analysis.valuation_read: At ₹675, DLF trades around 34-37x trailing earnings and roughly 3.3-3.6x book value - rich multiples next to an ROE under 10% and ROCE near 6-7%. Why it's expensive: the market appears to be pricing DLF less as a conventional low-return developer and more on the optionality of its rental annuity business - a ~50 million sq ft DCCDL portfolio at 96% occupancy, guided toward a ₹6,800 crore annual exit rental run-rate and a medium-term target near ₹10,000 crore - cash flows that don't fully show up in standalone profitability ratios. Whether that premium is actually earned depends on whether the ₹20,000 crore FY27 sales target and the rental ramp-up land on schedule; that execution has not yet been verified against results.
analysis.growth_read: This looks more mix-led than volume-led right now: quarterly booking volumes are running behind the pace needed for full-year guidance, reported revenue is distorted by recognition timing, and the steadiest source of profit growth is the rental annuity business rather than a clear jump in homes sold.
analysis.health_read: Financial risk looks low - standalone debt-to-equity is reported near zero, management cited a large cash reserve (around ₹15,100 crore mentioned on the earnings call) and operating cash flow of ₹1,858 crore for the quarter. The real question is business risk: whether enough homes sell at the right price to hit the ₹20,000 crore FY27 target, and whether 96% rental occupancy holds as the portfolio expands.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters held 74.08% as of the June 2026 quarter, unchanged quarter-on-quarter, and the promoter group formally declared zero encumbrance/pledge on its shares for FY26. FII holding dipped slightly (13.54% to 12.31%) while mutual funds added (5.15% to 6.12%). The board has also moved to reclassify promoter entity Madhukar Housing to the public category. Not verified - no well-known individual investor was found on DLF's public shareholder register; note that GIC's stake sits in the DCCDL joint venture, not in DLF's own listed equity, so it would not show up on DLF's shareholding pattern.
strengths: Consolidated Q2 FY27 PAT of ₹1,301 crore, up 11% YoY, holding up despite a recognition-driven dip in reported revenue
DCCDL rental annuity portfolio running at 96% occupancy by area with ₹1,482 crore quarterly rental income and ₹1,537 crore EBITDA
Standalone debt-to-equity near zero plus a large cash balance, giving the balance sheet real flexibility
Dividend per share raised every year from ₹1.2 (FY20) to ₹8 (FY26), even though the yield itself is modest at 1.18%
watchpoints: Q2 FY27 sales bookings of ₹3,800 crore are a small fraction of the ₹20,000 crore full-year target - H2 launches (Hamilton Court 2, Goa villas, Mumbai Westpark) have to deliver
ROE (~9.7%) and ROCE (~6.3-6.8%) are low relative to the ~34-37x earnings multiple the stock commands
Revenue recognition lumpiness (percentage-completion/possession-based) makes quarter-on-quarter top-line comparisons unreliable - bookings and PAT are the better signals
Even after strong 3-5 year outperformance, the stock remains 33% below the January 2008 peak set 19 years ago
analysis.one_thing: Whether new sales bookings actually ramp from ₹3,800 crore in Q2 toward the ₹20,000 crore FY27 target in the second half - on the back of the Hamilton Court 2, Goa villas and Mumbai Westpark launches - which would confirm the premium valuation is backed by execution rather than just the rental-annuity story.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 results (PAT, revenue, dividend, bookings), shareholding/pledge disclosures, and earnings-call rental/occupancy figures were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Business Standard, Zee Biz, Investing.com/GuruFocus, ScanX, Univest). Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE) varied slightly across Screener, Value Research and Tijori - the clustered range was used rather than a single outlier source. Exact consolidated net debt (as distinct from standalone debt-to-equity) and the presence/absence of any marquee individual investor were not independently verified - check on Screener or the latest exchange shareholding filing.
